ledgerCoverage.note: The repository ledger covers the indexed source universe. The records below are the pages and posts directly inspected for this content-seeding pass.

facts: The page identifies Fayette County Habitat for Humanity and links to legacy sections.
It displays 16 years serving, 9 homes built, 4 repair projects, 2,500+ volunteers and donors, and $1.2 million added to the tax base.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Metrics conflict with other legacy pages and have no methodology or as-of context.

facts: The page states the organization was founded in 2004 and lists 32 historical records with month/year, type, and community-level location.
The list includes Aging in Place, new-home work, critical home repair, community engagement, disaster response, and ramp installations.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Many entries are sparse and some associated media have unresolved rights, consent, or filename-only alt text.

facts: The page describes Fayette County Habitat for Humanity as a local nonprofit and says it has been part of the community for seventeen years.
It discusses affordable housing, collaboration, volunteer engagement, sustainability, and empowerment.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: The 17-year claim conflicts with the homepage and the page uses retired or non-preferred brand language.

facts: The page describes practical modifications including ramps, handrails, grab bars, lighting, and accessible bathrooms.
It displays a $5,000 cap, an 80% AMI threshold, repayment terms, zero interest, and funding-availability language.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Eligibility, financial, and availability details require current organizational verification; the linked assistance PDF requests SSNs and email submission.

facts: The page describes urgent repair examples such as a burst pipe, failing heater, fallen tree, or utility shutoff.
It displays a $1,000 cap, an 80% AMI threshold, repayment terms, zero interest, and funding-availability language.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Eligibility, financial, and availability details require current organizational verification; the linked assistance PDF requests SSNs and email submission.

facts: The page says applications were not currently being accepted at its crawl time and describes a future information-session process.
It displays 30–80% AMI guidance and household, credit, residence, and program-participation statements.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Applicant policy and intake details are changeable and private; the legacy process must not be reproduced.

facts: The page says the organization was not currently accepting applications for the home repair program at its crawl time.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: No existing public Program destination and no current intake verification.

facts: The page provides general volunteer participation guidance and points users to volunteer registration.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: The registration destination and workflow remain DonorView-owned and require account confirmation.

facts: The page contains general answers about Habitat and volunteer participation.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Copied legacy page and stale operational details; only verified, concise guidance may be transformed into the existing volunteer page.

facts: The page describes fundraising, family selection, construction, and communications/outreach committees.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Committee names, responsibilities, and recruitment state require current verification; family-selection language requires remediation.

facts: The page describes bequests, life insurance, stock, real estate, and consulting an advisor.
It includes a named contact, phone number, email address, and a linked intent form.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Legal/tax language, contact details, process, and form rights require verification; no current planned-giving destination exists.

facts: The page describes ReStore as a nonprofit home-improvement store and lists 825 N. Main St., Schulenburg, Texas 78945.
It lists Friday and Saturday donation and sale hours of 9:00am–1:00pm.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: The new site has no current ReStore destination; address and hours need current verification before any future use.

facts: The page contains donation guidance and outbound giving links.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: DonorView owns giving records and destinations; legacy URLs and attribution behavior cannot be assumed.

facts: The page describes Camp St. Cottages as an older-adult neighborhood concept in La Grange.
It is a candidate historical Project or Story source, but the page does not establish a current project status in the new model.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Needs factual status and outcome verification before a public Project or Story release.

facts: The page is a legacy index for posts and categories.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: It does not define the new Stories, News, taxonomy, or routes.

facts: The page describes a 2026 raffle with ticket pricing, a May 23, 2026 drawing, and prize values.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: The page has legal/compliance material and inconsistent or incomplete prize/timing details across related raffle pages.

facts: The page describes a 2026 raffle with a $100 ticket, a May 23, 2026 drawing, and a different stated drawing time from the Blueprint page.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Conflicting event editions/times, placeholder prize values, and legal review requirements block publication.

facts: The page contains event marketing copy and calls to reserve tickets, sponsor, or donate a prize.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: No current edition, dates, or verified destination are established.

facts: The page describes a Habitat booth at Bluff Schützenfest and lists food/service details.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Future event date, partner recognition, and external event destination require verification.

facts: The September 2021 post describes a planned 10-unit, 640-square-foot, ADA-compliant cottage concept and a September 10, 2021 public event.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: The post describes a plan, not an independently verified current outcome; associated image rights require review.

facts: The February 2025 post describes construction progress on a named household's home and mentions siding, volunteers, and construction participation.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Named household and minor details require current consent, privacy, and dignity review; source images require rights review.

inspectedPages.sourceTitle: Fayette County Habitat for Humanity Selects Partner Family for New Home Build
facts: The July 2023 post describes a selected household for a milestone tenth home build and includes household and program-participation details.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Participant consent, current privacy review, and conflict with the homepage's 9 homes built metric block direct migration.

facts: The July 2020 post invites residents to complete an anonymous housing survey and identifies housing-needs research as its purpose.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: No methodology, results, owner, or approved public metric destination is present in the new site.

inspectedPages.sourceTitle: Why Sweat Equity Matters: Building More Than Just Homes
facts: The post explains the legacy concept of sweat equity and connects it to Habitat participation.
inspectedPages.confidenceConcern: Legacy framing requires substantive language remediation and current policy verification before reuse.

inspectionNote: The full indexed ledger was reviewed for coverage and risk flags; direct content inspection focused on the source pages and posts with plausible destinations in the existing application. Legacy navigation and page hierarchy were not reproduced.
